subtopics.title: First and Second Differences — the Diagnosis

questions.question: A number pattern is quadratic exactly when:
options: Its terms are all perfect squares

questions.question: For 3; 8; 15; 24; 35, the first differences are:
The constant second difference of a quadratic pattern equals:
options: a — the coefficient of n² itself

questions.question: A second difference of −4 would tell you that:
options: The pattern is linear after all
a = −2, and the pattern eventually turns downward

questions.question: The three facts that pin down a, b and c are:
options: The last term, the sum of terms, and the product of terms
2a = second difference; 3a + b = first first-difference; a + b + c = T1
a = T1; b = T2; c = T3
The mean, median and mode of the sequence

For the dipping sequence 6; 3; 2; 3; 6, the general term works out to:
After building Tn, you should test it on:
options: No terms — the method guarantees it
A term of a different sequence
A term you did NOT use in the building

subtopics.title: Using the General Term in Both Directions

questions.question: For Tn = n² + 2n, the fiftieth term is:
Solving n² + 2n = 120 gives n = 10 or n = −12. The correct conclusion is:
options: Both the tenth term and the minus-twelfth term equal 120
The tenth term is 120; n = −12 is rejected because positions are positive whole numbers

questions.question: 200 is not a term of Tn = n² + 2n because:
options: The discriminant of n² + 2n − 200 = 0 is 804, not a perfect square, so no natural n exists
200 is smaller than the fiftieth term

questions.question: When a is negative, the pattern has:
options: A largest term at the turning point, after which it descends

subtopics.title: Patterns in Context — Tiles, Stacks and Real Counts

questions.question: The structural route reads Tn = n(n + 2) for the tile decks because figure n is:
options: A rectangle of n rows by n + 2 columns

questions.question: Figure 20 of the tile pattern uses:
The figure using exactly 224 tiles is found from n² + 2n − 224 = 0, giving:
A quick protection against a wrong formula in context questions is to:
options: Round every answer to the nearest ten
Assume the first figure uses one tile
Substitute back and confirm the formula reproduces figures 1 and 2 exactly

subtopics.title: The Fingerprint at the Second Layer

questions.question: In the staircase picture, quadratic growth feels like:
options: Every step taller than the last, but always by the same extra amount
Steps that shrink as you climb

questions.question: The steady second-layer number measures the pattern by giving:
options: The first term of the sequence

questions.question: A steady second difference of 6 means the pattern is built on:
Fingerprinting from only three terms is unsafe because:
options: Three terms take too long to difference
The second difference of three terms is always zero
Patterns never have exactly three terms
Three terms cannot commit a pattern — the steadiness must show itself more than once

questions.question: The correct order for finding the three coefficients is:
options: a from the second difference, then b from the first gap, then c from the first term
b first, because it is in the middle

questions.question: b cannot be found before a because:
options: a appears inside the equation 3a + b = first gap
The first gap depends on c

questions.question: If the assembled machine fails its test on an unseen term, the first suspect is:
options: a, because it was found first
The sequence itself, which must be wrong
c, because it absorbs arithmetic slips

questions.question: The dipping sequence 6; 3; 2; 3; 6 mirrors itself because:
options: It is a parabola sampled at whole numbers, symmetric about its lowest point at position 3
All quadratic patterns repeat every five terms

subtopics.title: Driving the Machine Forwards and in Reverse

questions.question: Driving forward means:
options: Feeding a position into Tn to receive the term's value
Solving a quadratic equation for n
Listing every term up to the one wanted

questions.question: Driving in reverse — from a value to its position — requires:
options: Dividing the value by the second difference
Setting Tn equal to the value and solving the quadratic equation
Subtracting the first term from the value

questions.question: The seat picture — seat 10 exists, seat minus 12 does not — reminds you to:
options: Round negative answers up to zero
Reject non-natural solutions for n, with a written reason
Count seats from the back of the taxi

questions.question: The staircase 'never touches 20' between 15 and 24 illustrates that:
options: Every whole number eventually appears in a pattern
A pattern only lands where its steps land — some values are simply never visited
